stories.title: Trump backed Nvidia's reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang, sources and officials say
new_facts: Trump told CNBC 'it's a threat to lose him'; affairs reportedly include a woman suspected of spying for China.
Trump and Vance personally intervened, convinced Huang alone protected American-made open-weight AI models.
Nvidia board reinstated Huang as CEO and president on Monday; stock rose over 30%; board statement cited his candor.
Nvidia market value soared by $1 trillion; Trump and tech figures applauded the return.
Sen. Ruben Gallego said Trump's role was close to 'socialism, communism' as he's ever seen.
Trump said Huang will emerge at a higher level and quipped 'sex sells' about the affair scandal.
Interim chief Kress and senior management were unaware of the weekend discussions on reinstating Huang.
Members of Congress from both parties criticize the reinstatement and question national security risks.
stories.line: Nvidia's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang after Trump reportedly pushed for it, drawing criticism over political influence in a major AI company.

stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO despite espionage concerns
new_facts: Huang returned to Nvidia leadership under two weeks after his ousting; politicians in both parties reacted with anger and shock.
Nvidia board reinstated Huang as CEO; S&P 500 rose nearly 5% and Dow jumped over 1,500 points Monday.
Nvidia board approved Huang's return as CEO; Nasdaq fell 10% last week, its worst week since 2020.
Lawmakers of both parties still expect Huang to answer questions on Capitol Hill next week.
stories.line: Nvidia's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang after his ouster over affairs, one tied to a suspected Chinese spy, drawing congressional scrutiny.

Trump-backed Nvidia reinstatement of Huang draws bipartisan fury; Megaspeed added to trade blacklist
new_facts: Commerce to add Singapore-based Megaspeed to trade blacklist, requiring licenses for US chip sales to it.
Names Alice Huang as the suspected Chinese intelligence asset; gives Nov. 12 as the resignation date.
House Democratic leader Jeffries called the return 'indefensible' and urged ironclad chip export controls in the defense policy bill.
Megaspeed International, a Singapore firm, is the company at the center of the scandal, with alleged chip smuggling into China.
US is investigating Megaspeed and Alice Huang; a former associate of hers was reportedly 'deeply involved' in the firm.
US intelligence reportedly shows Alice Huang was in contact with China's Ministry of State Security during her relationship with Huang.
stories.line: Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang after he resigned over an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy; the US is blacklisting an affiliated chip firm.

stories.title: Don Toliver Manchester concert evacuated after unknown substance hits crowd
new_facts: First report: over 12,000 evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live arena after an unknown substance was released at a concert.
Names Don Toliver as performer, ushered off stage Sunday night; he postponed his O2 gig.
Over 80 people treated by medics; authorities in Manchester described an unknown irritant, speaking Monday.
stories.line: A U.S. rapper's Manchester concert was evacuated after an unknown substance, possibly tear gas, hit a crowd of 12,000; dozens were assessed.

stories.title: Analysis estimates over 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
new_facts: NYT analysis of hacked government data estimates over 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war.
DNI Jay Clayton named acting national cyber director, replacing Sean Cairncross, whom Trump said was not good enough.
Tajikistan began withdrawing from the ICC during Putin's visit, as the US calls for the court to be dismantled.
ICC found Tajikistan failed to comply with its request to arrest Putin.
Trump reposted an AI video on Truth Social at 6:30 a.m. Monday showing his China trip and trilateral summit with Putin and Xi.
DNI Clayton gave an evasive response when pressed on whether Putin is a friend, after Trump called Putin a friend.
stories.line: An independent analysis estimates over 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; national security questions remain
new_facts: Trump says he spoke to Xi about Huang, that Huang did nothing wrong, and that the board sought assurances.
Trump cited the US attorney general in defending Huang and urged Nvidia to continue its export-control investigation.
One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a direct report.
Reports claim Huang had affairs with at least three women, including the suspected Chinese spy.
A probe into Huang's conduct is ongoing despite his reinstatement.
stories.line: Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang amid unresolved questions about national security risks, after an intelligence-related scandal.

stories.title: Trump halts Army detonation of unstable explosives at Iowa plant pending court approval
new_facts: Trump says Army should delay detonating a cache of dangerous explosives in Iowa until a legal challenge is decided.
Trump says he will wait for courts and Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand to agree with the Army's plan.
The material is drums of lead azide stored in a bunker at an Iowa army facility.
Community outcry over toxic lead dust plume risk across parts of Iowa and Illinois; detonation is the subject of a court battle.
68 barrels of lead azide; detonation first planned for Friday, with the date changed three times after public concern.
Army again postponed the detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, now scheduled for Nov. 25.
Army planned to detonate Wednesday despite a court order seeking to stop it; plume could disperse across much of the Midwest.
stories.line: Trump has ordered the Army to pause a planned detonation of unstable explosive chemicals at an Iowa facility pending court approval.
